sentences.text: Dysmoropelia dekarchiskos is the only species within its genus, making it a monotypic group.
This large dove measured approximately 31 cm in length and possessed robust legs with wings that were short relative to its body.
Its physical adaptations resemble those of other flightless Columbidae, such as the dodo, though these traits were less extreme.
The genus name combines Greek words meaning 'unfortunate' and 'wild dove'.
The species name honors Napoleon Bonaparte's exile, referencing Greek terms for 'leader of ten men' and 'small cape'.
Olson described this bird in 1975, placing it in the family Columbidae and the order Columbiformes.
Fossils recovered from the Sugarloaf Hill locality were preserved in aeolian calcareous sands.
The bird lived exclusively on Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean between 0.129 and 0.0117 million years ago.
Some researchers presume the bird was hunted to extinction shortly after the island was discovered in 1502.
